title: Home Comfort Financing Late Fee Posting — Servicing Reference
content:
**Servicing reference card — Home Comfort Financing late fees.**

## When a late fee is charged

A late fee is charged on a Home Comfort Financing account for every statement period whose required payment is still unpaid more than the plan's late-fee grace period (in calendar days) after its due date, at most one for each statement period, and it is posted on the first day after that period's statement closes.

| Question | Answer under this rule |
|---|---|
| Which statement periods carry a late fee? | every statement period whose required payment is still unpaid more than the grace period after its due date |
| How many late fees can one statement period carry? | at most one |
| When is it posted? | on the first day after that period's statement closes |
| What does posting do? | the late fee is added to what the borrower owes, appears on that month's statement as a late fee line, and the balance rises by the same amount |

Statements close on the last day of each calendar month, so the first day after a period's statement closes is the first day of the following month.

## Posting the fee: `post_late_fee_ce58c754`

**Capability.** `post_late_fee_ce58c754` posts a late fee on a Home Comfort Financing account for one statement month. The fee is added to the amount the borrower owes on the account, appears on that month's statement as a late fee line dated today, and the account balance rises by the same amount. The tool books the amount it is given; it does not work out the fee.

**How it is invoked.** It is an agent-side tool: the agent unlocks `post_late_fee_ce58c754` and then calls it.

**Parameters.**

| Parameter | What it is | Format |
|---|---|---|
| `finance_account_id` | reference number of the financing account the late fee is charged to, as shown by the financing account lookup for the verified borrower | identifier, as shown in the lookup |
| `statement_period` | the statement month the late fee belongs to | YYYY-MM (four-digit year, hyphen, two-digit month, e.g. 2026-04), in Eastern time |
| `amount` | the late fee to post | USD, 2 decimal places, always positive, already rounded to the cent |

**Return.** On success the receipt carries `finance_txn_id` (reference number of the new late fee line), `line_type` (always `late_fee`), `statement_period` (the YYYY-MM month the fee was posted to), `amount` (USD, 2 decimal places), `posted_date` (YYYY-MM-DD posting date), `account_balance` (USD, 2 decimal places, the balance owed after the fee) and `status`. The call has succeeded when `status` comes back as "posted".

## Input and receipt — illustration (hypothetical values)

Called with `finance_account_id` of a borrower's account, `statement_period` 2026-04 and `amount` 25.00, on an account whose balance was $3120.40, the receipt shows `line_type` `late_fee`, `statement_period` 2026-04, `amount` 25.00, today's `posted_date`, `account_balance` 3145.40 and `status` "posted".
